content:
Apple today released the fifth beta of iOS 27 along with companion updates, but at the same time also launched unexpected second-wave beta versions including iOS 26.6.1 and macOS 26.6.2.

iOS 26.6.1, iPadOS 26.6.1, and macOS 26.6.2 beta versions arrive

If you've been using Apple's beta software, you have two choices today.

After a three-week wait, the fifth beta of iOS 27 has finally arrived, marking Apple's ongoing summer preparations for its next major software release.

But Apple has also just rolled out a new round of beta versions for iOS 26 and its companion updates.

The first betas of iOS 26.6.1, iPadOS 26.6.1, and macOS 26.6.2 are now available.

Apple typically doesn't offer beta versions for these smaller updates, instead choosing to push them out immediately without prior notice.

These updates could potentially replace larger updates like iOS 26.7. But regardless of the reason, Apple clearly felt it necessary to release these new iOS 26 updates as betas first before making them available to the public.

The iOS 26.6.1 updates and similar releases are expected to contain only security updates and bug fixes. If any specific changes are discovered, we will continue to report on them.

Note: If you've already upgraded your iPhone to the iOS 27 beta, you won't see the option to install iOS 26.6.1. That update is only for devices still running iOS 26.

Are you still on iOS 26? Have you noticed any differences in the iOS 26.6.1 beta? Let us know in the comments.
